idiom_name: case class snapshots + immutable SortedMap[LocalDate, Version] with rangeTo as-of lookup
implementation_notes: Case classes provide the version role (immutable vals plus copy for the working copy) and scala.collection.immutable.SortedMap provides the temporal collection: as-of is history.rangeTo(on).lastOption, current is history.last, and an amendment is history + (effective -> working) - one line each, no search code. Vector plus binarySearch is the alternative for short or strictly append-only histories, and an Ordering for the key is what makes the range queries work. In a persisted model the same shape is a version table keyed (id, effective_date) with Slick/doobie/ORM mapping rows to case-class versions.
code_sketch:
final case class Version(effective: LocalDate, terms: Terms)        // immutable version

final class Contract(history: SortedMap[LocalDate, Version]) {       // continuity
  def current: Version = history.last._2
  def asOf(on: LocalDate): Option[Version] = history.rangeTo(on).lastOption  // None = Missing
  def amend(effective: LocalDate, working: Terms): Contract =
    Contract(history + (effective -> Version(effective, working)))
}
pitfalls: case class copy() is shallow: a List or Map member is shared with the previous version, so mutating it rewrites history - keep fields immutable values or copy collections when publishing.

SortedMap range queries need an Ordering for the key; LocalDate is ISO-chronological, but switching to Instant/LocalDateTime or a custom key without a matching Ordering changes the lookup semantics or fails to compile.
Ordering is not the same as equality: an Ordering inconsistent with equals breaks SortedMap lookups and can let two keys that compare equal coexist as separate versions.
LocalDate is timezone-free while the persistence layer usually writes UTC timestamps - storing LocalDate keys over UTC instants shifts effective dates by the server offset.
